entries.title: II Timothy 1:1
segments: The life. The spiritual life, or life eternal.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:3
segments: In a pure conscience.  However far from the truth Paul had been before his conversion he had lived up to the best that he knew, under the guidance of a pure conscience.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:6
segments: Laying on of my hands. See note

entries.title: II Timothy 1:7
segments: Fearfulness.  Perhaps referring to the authority of the Jewish law which was upheld by fear of the penalties threatened.  In a wider sense it may be taken as the fear of the powers of darkness (
), as opposed to the power of God.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:8
segments:
Testimony of our Lord. Bearing witness to faith in Christ.
 

 
 His prisoner. Paul was suffering his second imprisonment at Rome at the time this epistle was written.

entries.title: II Timothy 1:9
segments: Before times eternal. The grace of Christ was really bestowed upon mankind under the old covenant, but became manifest only under the new covenant of the gospel.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:10
segments: Abolished death. By his resurrection in the body Christ had proved death conquerable.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:12
segments: That which I have committed. The great desire of the Jews was for eternal life (
), and in the faith that Christ was the way (

), he committed his life here and hereafter wholly and unreservedly to his service.
 

 
 That day. The day of Christ's coming.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:13
segments: The pattern. The oft-repeated injunction of Paul to cling to the original teachings of the gospel, indicates the great variance which seemed to be continually leading would-be followers into fatal error.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:16
segments: The house of Onesiphorus. As only his house is mentioned it must be concluded that Onesiphorus himself had passed away.  See

entries.title: II Timothy 1:18
segments: Thou knowest. Timothy had spent more time than Paul had at Ephesus.
